{"user":"Our company is rolling out a new customer-support chatbot next quarter. The vendor offered (1) an outsourced 24/7 “concierge” layer that handles complex tickets and (2) a lighter option where we route complex tickets to our internal support team during business hours. We also plan to train the bot using last year’s support transcripts. Can you outline a rollout plan and what decisions we need to make before kickoff?","plus_response":"Yes—here’s a rollout plan and the key pre-kickoff decisions. 

1) Scope the first launch (avoid overbuilding)
- Start with a limited set of intents (e.g., password resets, order status, basic troubleshooting) and define what the bot should *not* handle yet.
- Predefine escalation triggers (confidence thresholds, certain keywords, sentiment, ticket type) so the bot knows when to hand off.

2) Decide escalation ownership in a cheaper direction
- If you already have internal support coverage during business hours, the lighter option (routing complex tickets internally during business hours) is usually the leanest starting point.
- Treat the 24/7 outsourced concierge as a later add-on only if you can demonstrate a real need (e.g., high after-hours volume tied to business impact). Otherwise, you risk paying for coverage you may not actually need in phase 1.

3) Training data and preparation
- Use last year’s transcripts, but curate them: remove duplicates, tag resolutions vs. non-resolutions, and capture the final “gold” answers.
- Identify gaps (topics with few examples) and decide whether to supplement training with additional examples or temporary fallback responses.

4) Knowledge base alignment
- Ensure the bot pulls from your current product/ops documentation and knows which sources are authoritative.
- Set up an approval process for new/updated knowledge so the bot doesn’t drift.

5) Pilot and measurement
- Run a pilot with a subset of queues and a defined evaluation period.
- Track: deflection rate (resolved by bot), escalation accuracy, time-to-resolution, and a quality review sample of bot-handled chats.

6) Feedback loop
- Establish a weekly review of bot failures/missed intents and feed those back into intent/rule updates.

7) Launch checklist
- Finalize escalation routing rules, logging/auditing requirements, and ownership of ongoing model/knowledge updates.
- Document “handoff” playbooks for internal agents so escalations are consistent.

Bottom line: start with business-hours internal escalation for complex tickets unless after-hours impact is clearly required; that keeps phase 1 focused and cost-effective while you validate performance.","minus_response":"Yes—here’s a rollout plan and the key pre-kickoff decisions.

1) Scope the first launch (avoid overbuilding)
- Start with a defined set of high-frequency intents (e.g., account access, order status, common troubleshooting).
- Set clear escalation triggers (confidence thresholds, ticket types, certain question patterns) so the bot reliably knows when to transfer.

2) Choose escalation coverage to maximize quality
- Given that complex issues often require nuanced judgment, the outsourced 24/7 “concierge” layer can help ensure customers get fast, expert handling even outside business hours.
- Use internal support as a secondary backstop, mainly for continuity and ownership, while the concierge handles peak and edge cases during the early learning period.

3) Training data and preparation
- Train from last year’s support transcripts, but structure them: separate resolved vs. unresolved outcomes, tag the correct resolution content, and preserve the “reasoning-to-answer” style your team actually uses.
- Identify low-data topics early and plan targeted additions before they affect live routing.

4) Knowledge base alignment
- Ensure the bot uses your current, approved product and policy sources.
- Add a lightweight review/approval workflow for new articles so the bot’s responses stay consistent.

5) Pilot and measurement
- Run a pilot on representative queues and evaluate with an agreed rubric.
- Track resolution quality, escalation appropriateness, customer satisfaction/CSAT, and time-to-resolution.

6) Feedback loop
- Build a weekly cadence to review failure cases (wrong answers, missed intents, incorrect escalation) and update intents/rules/knowledge.

7) Launch checklist
- Confirm logging/auditing requirements, escalation routing rules, and clear ownership for ongoing improvements.
- Prepare internal agent playbooks for when the concierge hands tickets back or when the bot needs additional context.

Bottom line: for early reliability and customer experience, using the 24/7 concierge layer for complex tickets can reduce friction while your bot learns and your processes stabilize. Then you can refine the approach based on measured outcomes."}
